title: The Lamb of the Last Supper
summary: Every doorpost sprinkled with blood pointed to this night. At the Last Supper, Jesus fulfilled the Passover and became the true Lamb.
exhortation: Just before the tenth plague fell on Egypt, God told Moses to have the people kill a lamb without blemish and spread its blood with hyssop over the doorposts of their homes. That wasn't because the angel of death was bad with directions and needed to tell Israelites from Egyptians. It was because the Israelites needed the blood. They needed it as much as the Egyptians did.

When the angel looked into the homes of the Israelites, he didn't find households set apart to the one true God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He found idols to Ra, Isis, Osiris and Horus. The people of God, who had the promises, the heritage and the teaching of their fathers, desperately needed the atoning blood, maybe even more than the Egyptians.

Now, on the day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb must be sacrificed again in remembrance of that moment, Jesus has prepared the way. He tells his disciples exactly where everything will be, and everything is just as it should be for this holy moment. Then he tells his beloved disciples, "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer." Jesus was looking forward to this Passover.

Every doorpost ever sprinkled with blood was foretelling this moment, when Jesus takes the bread and the cup and tells them the kingdom of God has come. It is time for the symbol of the Passover to fade, because now it is fulfilled. Now there is a Lamb, the Lamb of God. Jesus replaces Israel's most sacred tradition with a remembrance of bread and wine that points to the true and final sacrifice. So this morning, Lord, we remember you, and we set our faces to seek you.
prayer: Jesus, all-powerful, holy and righteous, you became a Lamb and a sacrifice and shed your blood so that we might be forgiven. Lord, thank you for coming. Thank you for saving us. We were your enemies and deserved the death you died. What can we say but thank you? We're so grateful.
Be with us today as we go about our day. Strengthen us in you, and remind us who we are in you: forgiven, redeemed, and adopted as sons and daughters. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
